requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to its declaration or within its body. A named example MUST cite a requirement. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count. Habeas MUST report every uncited function with its file, line, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation matches the requirement text, and the tests cover the main cases. I did not run the tests or the repository self-validation; the self-validation point rests on reading the code and a spot-check.

**Wiring.** `inspect_repository` in `src/evidence.rs` calls `crate::rust_coverage::validate_rust_functions` during repository validation. That call carries its own `{impl}` comment.

**Parsing every first-party file.**
- `rust_files` walks the whole project tree.
  - It skips `.git` and `target` at any depth.
  - It skips `book`, `evidence` and `vendor` only at the root, so `src/evidence/check.rs` is still scanned.
- `validate_rust_functions` reads each file and calls `missing_function_references`, which runs `syn::parse_file`.
- A parse failure becomes `"{file}:{line}: cannot parse Rust source: …"`, and read or directory errors are also reported. Files are never silently skipped.

**Which functions are collected.**
- `FunctionCollector` visits `ItemFn`, `ImplItemFn`, `TraitItemFn` and `ForeignItemFn`, and recurses into each. That covers free functions, methods, trait methods (including bodiless ones), extern functions, nested functions and test helpers.
- Functions generated inside macros are not seen. That fits "explicitly declared".

**Which comments count.**
- `comments()` is a lexer that skips string, raw-string, byte-string and char literals, so a reference in a string literal does not count. It also handles nested block comments.
- `attached_comment_indices` attaches comments that sit directly above a function with at most one blank line and nothing else between them. A comment is not attached if code precedes it on its line, or if it is an inner doc comment (`//!` or `/*!`).
- A comment inside a function's span goes to the smallest enclosing function, so a comment in a nested function does not credit the outer one.
- Comments on an enclosing `mod` or `impl` only count if they are directly attached to a function, which in practice excludes them.
- A reference counts only if its role is not `term` and it names a defined requirement or example. Unknown names do not count.
- Uncited functions are reported with file, line and name.
- Citations are not checked by definition kind. A named example that cites no requirement still counts here, but the definition-collection check in `src/evidence.rs` reports that separately ("example … must cite at least one requirement").

**Tests in `src/rust_coverage.rs`.**
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - enclosing mod and impl references not counting;
  - string and raw-string references not counting;
  - unknown names not counting;
  - body block comments counting;
  - a distant comment not counting;
  - a trailing comment on the previous line not counting;
  - an inner doc comment not counting;
  - an outer doc comment counting.
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, `{test}` references on a requirement and on a named example, and an uncited test helper.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks byte-offset and line handling.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` checks multi-file traversal, nested directories, a parse failure, and the `target` and root `evidence` exclusions.

**Integration tests.**
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs::discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference` checks the parse-failure diagnostic through the CLI.
- `tests/commands.rs::status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form` checks the "has no requirement or example citation" message through the CLI.
- `tests/habeas.rs` runs `habeas::validate()` on the repository itself. The visible sampled functions are cited, e.g. `fn habeas` carries `{test}\`requirements.integration.self_test\``.

**Minor observations, not gaps.**
- No test exercises `ForeignItemFn` specifically.
- The reported line for a function with attributes is the start of its span, which includes the attributes.

No FIXME-acknowledged gaps were found in `src/rust_coverage.rs`.

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to its declaration or within its body. A named example MUST cite a requirement. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count. Habeas MUST report every uncited function with its file, line, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.

A definition glob MUST match a complete full name. `*` MUST match zero or more characters, including dots; all other valid name characters MUST match literally. An empty glob MUST be invalid. The same glob matching rule MUST be used by requirements evidence inputs and CLI definition filters. All three MUST match against both requirements and named examples.

Habeas MUST identify a Rust item by the pair of its repository-relative `rust_file` and a `rust_item` selector derived from a `syn` parse of that file. The selector MUST describe syntactic ancestry within the file and MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files or use line numbers as identity. Named items MUST use kind-and-name segments such as `fn[run]` and `struct[Packet]`. Impl segments MUST distinguish inherent from trait impls using their syntactic self type and optional trait path. Otherwise identical selectors MUST have deterministic source-order disambiguators. A `use` declaration MUST have a positional selector `use#N`, where N is its one-based position among sibling `use` declarations; its import target MUST NOT form part of the selector. Other items without a suitable name MUST have a kind and positional disambiguator. Selector spelling MUST be documented and reversible when names or types contain delimiter characters.
